nodes.label: Frozen HMAC timestamp on a client built once outside the poll loop
nodes.norm_label: frozen hmac timestamp on a client built once outside the poll loop
nodes.summary: Primary root cause of the two-way Telegram image sync bug: start_telegram_sync_worker builds its reqwest client once, outside its infinite loop, so build_client's HMAC timestamp is frozen at app startup while the Cloudflare proxy enforces a 300-second clock-skew window. Pairing survives because poll_pairing builds a fresh client per call.

nodes.label: Two distinct 401 bodies as a proxy-vs-Telegram rejection discriminator
nodes.norm_label: two distinct 401 bodies as a proxy vs telegram rejection discriminator
nodes.summary: Live read-only probe of the real proxy with a bogus token, varying only the timestamp age: 0 s returns Telegram's JSON invalid-token body (proxy forwarded), 3600 s returns the proxy's plain-text Unauthorized Proxy Access, 200 s is inside the window. The two distinct bodies are what separate proxy rejection from Telegram rejection.

nodes.label: Linux-only stale Magic Menu cache from a Windows-gated invalidation
nodes.norm_label: linux only stale magic menu cache from a windows gated invalidation
nodes.summary: Second, independent cause: invalidate_clipboard_menu() sits inside a #[cfg(target_os = "windows")] handler and add_clipboard_entry clears only the history cache, while the menu cache is served unfiltered and has no expiry check. The inserted row is correct in the DB but a warmed Magic Menu keeps serving the stale list.

nodes.label: Bare base64 in the DB prefixed at render is the correct pairing
nodes.norm_label: bare base64 in the db prefixed at render is the correct pairing
nodes.summary: DB forensics on the real snipset.db: all 56 image rows hold bare base64 with zero data: prefixes while all three renderers prepend data:image/png;base64, unconditionally, and the one Telegram-sourced row's bytes are a real JFIF JPEG. The representation-mismatch hypothesis was therefore disproved, not confirmed.

nodes.label: Browser sniffing overrides the declared image MIME subtype
nodes.norm_label: browser sniffing overrides the declared image mime subtype
nodes.summary: External-evidence chunk C14 found that WHATWG HTML image-sniffing and MIME Sniffing let the browser detect the real type from bytes and override the declared subtype, so send_photo's hardcoded image/png never broke rendering. That reclassified F6 as correctness hygiene rather than the reported bug, and also showed Telegram's getFile preserves no MIME type, so F6 must sniff bytes.

nodes.label: A compile-failure RED takes down the whole crate's suite and proves nothing
nodes.norm_label: a compile failure red takes down the whole crate suite and proves nothing
nodes.summary: The first RED design asserted a seam that does not exist yet, so it failed to compile against the unpatched code. That would have taken the crate's 3,000+ tests down with it, making the failure indistinguishable from a build error. The corrected design proves RED behaviourally: the new test stays compiled while only the production fix is reverted.

nodes.label: Regression guard proven to fail on the reverted production fix
nodes.norm_label: regression guard proven to fail on the reverted production fix
nodes.summary: The first repro test passed with the bug present, discovered by reverting F1 on the VPS and seeing all 55 tests stay green. It was replaced first by a documented source-shape guard, then by an injectable acquisition seam, and the replacement was proved by simulating the regression on the VPS: the test failed naming the defect, then passed again on revert.

nodes.label: Verification run against an incomplete remote tree
nodes.norm_label: verification run against an incomplete remote tree
nodes.summary: The VPS build host was missing telegram_service_tests.rs and telegram_service_audit_tests.rs entirely, because the plan's T8 git checkout reverted them and a later scp transferred only two files using relative remote paths. A telegram-filtered run reported 34 tests where 55 should exist. Caused by under-reported test counts rather than lost tests; re-synced all seven changed files and re-verified.

nodes.label: Unbounded per-IP rate-limit map in the proxy worker
nodes.norm_label: unbounded per ip rate limit map in the proxy worker
nodes.summary: The Cloudflare proxy worker's rateHits map was never pruned, so every distinct client IP left a permanent entry. Fixed with a threshold-gated sweep that reuses the same expiry predicate as the lookup, so the two cannot drift semantically.
